gateway_facts_140_205.G1: 151-157: The status file is written only if TELEMETRY_STATUS_JSON is set. status is 'closed' only if the gateway started, shutdown gathered no errors, dropped and write_errors are falsy, and diagnostics (if present) are complete; otherwise it is 'failed'. dropped and write_errors are always recorded.
gateway_facts_140_205.G2: 161-173: The mpc_* keys exist only when MPC_OWNER_LEDGER_ENABLED. mpc_producer_final_sequence = mpc_sequence, mpc_remaining_requests = len(mpc_requests), mpc_unflushed_records = len(telemetry.records). The initial complete = (len(mpc_requests) == current_in_flight) and fsum(open costs) isclose current_admitted_cost (rel 1e-12, abs 1e-9). status becomes 'failed' if not complete or current_in_flight != 0.
gateway_facts_140_205.G3: 174-205: persist_status (ledger enabled) rereads the telemetry JSONL. Every row must carry this run_id, and each mpc_ledger row needs ledger_schema_version 2 and an int sequence == previous + 1, starting at 1. mpc_ledger_complete &= contiguous and last_sequence == producer and no unflushed records; otherwise status is set to 'failed'. It adds telemetry_file_sha256/bytes, mpc_final_sequence = last ledger sequence (0 if there are no ledger rows) and mpc_ledger_rows_written.
implications: I1: Any mpc_ledger row makes mpc_final_sequence >= 1, so the old body-run zero-sequence terms fail for every run that writes ledger rows (prior B2 effect is HIGH for such runs). Whether each MPC request emits ledger rows is decided outside 140-205 and is UNVERIFIED. U3 is therefore only partly resolved, but it no longer matters: the new body predicate is correct for 0 and for n >= 1.

I2: In a gateway-written, ledger-enabled status, 'closed' together with mpc_ledger_complete true already implies final == producer, unflushed == 0, current_in_flight == 0 (hence remaining == 0), and dropped/write_errors falsy. The explicit smoke terms are defense in depth and fail closed for a status this path did not produce (ledger disabled leaves the mpc_* keys absent; a status written before persist_status lacks mpc_final_sequence).
I3: The gateway tolerates float residue in current_admitted_cost (abs_tol 1e-9 at 164-165), so an exact == 0 drain test on admitted cost may fail spuriously after traffic.
I4: The status write site and its atomicity (after line 205) are UNVERIFIED.

l5_erratum.prior_text: REPORT findings_low L5 fix: 'Pass expected[clock_domain] (source-time, readiness-verified against the gateway at smoke 201-203).'
l5_erratum.status: WITHDRAWN: technically wrong; must not be implemented
l5_erratum.reason: capture_replay requires exact equality with the recorder label (C1-C3). expected['clock_domain'] is the gateway/SDK label ('linux-monotonic:...', Mayor-supplied; consistent with the prior REPORT, where it is the value checked against the gateway at smoke 201-203). That is a different label for the same physical clock. A 'linux-monotonic:' string can never equal one starting 'time.monotonic ', so the change would make every capture_replay refuse before any offer. That is fail-closed, but the run is certainly wasted. The prior fix conflated label equality with clock identity.
l5_erratum.corrected_position: No L5 code change is required. Passing the recorder label (the envelope's own capture['clock_domain'] or nominal_client.clock_domain()) is correct; the check is a same-host/boot consistency check by design and may be vacuous (INFO). Do NOT require replacing the recorder label with the SDK label or source. Permit, runtime and gateway checks keep their own namespace (prior V5, V6). Any same-physical-clock statement must cite source (time.monotonic implementation vs the SDK clock source), never label equality. Optional, not a gate: record both labels side by side.

b2_requirements.pass_if: With body None, the old smoke 314-318 predicate is unchanged or strictly stronger: status 'closed', mpc_ledger_complete true, and dropped, write_errors, mpc_remaining_requests, mpc_unflushed_records, mpc_final_sequence and mpc_producer_final_sequence all == 0, with the same failure reason.

Control: an equal nonzero pair passes. Each of the following fails: unequal, negative, bool or float sequences; complete false; status 'failed'; any nonzero counter.

b3_requirements.requirement: Offered accounting from real envelopes (old qualification 78-80)
b3_requirements.pass_if: No offered field is ever assigned from the plan or trace; planned sizes use distinct keys (e.g. episode_trace_requests). After prepare_episode returns, every exit from collect() (return or raise) sets offered_requests_from_driver = len(records) of the in-memory episode envelope (prepared.recorder.capture, mutated in place by capture_replay), or 0 if the envelope or records is None. Any warmup offered count likewise comes from the warmup envelope. This is the recorder's offered cohort (one record per accepted offer, each with a fate), not 'sent'. SHOULD: exits before prepare_episode set 0 together with the stage.
b3_requirements.fail_if: The 78-80 pre-set, or any plan-derived offered value (including a constant warmup count), survives on any path.

b3_requirements.requirement: NOT_RUN receipt for early exits (critical-path concern)
b3_requirements.pass_if: A try/finally covers from the return of prepare_episode (SHOULD: also prepare raising) to the await of run_episode. An entered flag is set as the last statement before that await, with no intervening await. If not entered, the finally writes an exclusive episode-not-run receipt via services.write (key redaction). It contains: stage; primary exception type and message; prepared.error; envelope status and error; records count 0; the PreparedCapture.started flag if available (client 862; must be False); sent 0. It also persists the prepared capture to a distinct exclusive path, unless adapter prepare-time persistence (U1) is proven by a sealed control. If entered, no NOT_RUN receipt is written (adapter run-time persistence owns that path). Control: an exception injected after prepare (prepared.error refusal, admin GET failure, pre-drain nonzero, permit coverage refusal, NominalRuntime raise) gives offered 0, a receipt, no capture_replay and no POST.
b3_requirements.fail_if: An early exit leaves no receipt, a receipt is written after run_episode was entered, or receipt values are derived from the plan.

b3_requirements.requirement: Primary exception preserved (L2: warmup finally old 55-64 and the new episode finally)
b3_requirements.pass_if: A persist or receipt write failure is recorded (report errors or a write-error file) and never replaces an in-flight primary exception. The primary propagates as the same object, with type and message intact. BaseException (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit, CancelledError) is never converted to Exception. With no primary, a persist failure still fails closed (V1). Controls: primary plus write failure; KeyboardInterrupt plus write failure.
b3_requirements.fail_if: The write exception surfaces instead of the primary, the primary is missing from the report, or an interrupt is downgraded.

b3_requirements.requirement: Pre-traffic pins (B1 residual, L6; old qualification 28, 35)
b3_requirements.pass_if: Before the first capture_replay (the warmup), the caller durably records two things. (a) The sha256 of the protocol bytes it parses (one read; hash and parse the same bytes), compared with the smoke startup pin (old smoke 118-121); a mismatch is refused before any offer. (b) sha256 and resolved path of its own file and of the nominal_episode module actually imported (module object __file__). SHOULD: strict parse (duplicate keys and non-finite constants rejected), and compare the adapter hash with a prereg-supplied expected pin when given.
b3_requirements.fail_if: Hash and parse use different reads, pins are recorded after traffic, or a mismatch does not refuse. Self-recorded hashes are evidence; the Mayor prereg pin (B1 PRECONDITION) remains the authority.

b3_requirements.requirement: Bounded pre/post drain and fallback counter (L4; client NOT_CLIENT_OWNED 101, 106)
b3_requirements.pass_if: A pre-drain runs after the warmup and before S is chosen; a post-drain runs after run_episode returns or raises. Each is a bounded /metrics read (B3-6) that persists the redacted snapshot and requires: in-flight == 0, waiting == 0 and tokenizer fallback requests == 0 (exact integers), and admitted cost == 0 or a pre-registered |x| <= 1e-9 (I3). A pre-drain failure refuses before S and the permit (NOT_RUN, B3-2). A post-drain failure or skip marks the episode not successful and never replaces a primary exception.
b3_requirements.fail_if: A drain is missing, a wait is unbounded, or success is reported with nonzero or unread counters. Only current_in_flight and current_admitted_cost are named in gateway 163-165; the waiting and fallback key names are UNVERIFIED here and must be bound to gateway source at acceptance.

b3_requirements.requirement: Positive, deadline-bounded GET timeouts (L7; old qualification 93)
b3_requirements.pass_if: Immediately before each GET, the budget is computed on time.monotonic from the original absolute deadlines: pre-traffic and pre-drain GETs against D - R; the post-drain GET against D - R or, if pre-registered, inside the reserve but never past D. If the budget is <= 0, no GET is issued and a refusal (or NOT_PERFORMED) is recorded; otherwise timeout = min(cap, budget).
b3_requirements.fail_if: A timeout <= 0 is possible, a GET is issued past its bound, or wall-clock time is mixed with the monotonic D/R.

b3_requirements.requirement: Same S/D/R and external authority (L9, L1; prior V2, V4)
b3_requirements.pass_if: Exactly one episode S (monotonic) feeds describe_protocol start_at, the permit (via the protocol sha), NominalRuntime start_at and run_episode offered_start; S is never retimed and there is no second S. The original owner.deadline and owner.reserve go unchanged to the warmup and episode paths. Before minting the permit, the caller checks not_before <= S < expires_at, S + max(episode_s, trace duration_seconds) <= min(D - R, expires_at) and window <= 60 s, and otherwise refuses before traffic. approved=True is set only under --execute, with the external prereg authority reference. Permit limits (window, max_commands, budgets) are not widened unless pre-registered and recorded. SHOULD (L1): record S - now at each pre-start stage.
b3_requirements.fail_if: S is recomputed or retimed, D or R is replaced, the permit is minted without the coverage check, or a new self-authorization path appears.

b3_requirements.requirement: Strict-JSON adapter result (L3; old qualification 128, smoke 327)
b3_requirements.pass_if: The report stores only a strict-JSON copy (json.dumps(sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False) inside a try, then json.loads). On failure it stores a safe summary (error type and message, str keys) and the episode is not successful. Control: a NaN or non-JSON value leaves the terminal report.json writable.
b3_requirements.fail_if: The raw adapter object is stored in report.

b3_requirements.requirement: Recorder clock label at capture_replay (L5 guard; see l5_erratum)
b3_requirements.pass_if: Every capture_replay call receives the recorder label (capture['clock_domain'] or nominal_client.clock_domain(); C1-C3). Permit, runtime and gateway checks keep the SDK namespace (prior V5, V6).
b3_requirements.fail_if: An SDK/gateway label (expected['clock_domain'] or the gateway state label) is passed to capture_replay or compared with a recorder label, or capture['clock_domain'] is rewritten.

b3_requirements.pass_if: The diff touches only the qualification and its test. Sends, schedule, request bodies, fates, the accepted client/metrics/adapter/runtime/permit bytes, and the warmup D/R/persistence (V1, V2) are unchanged. All new writes go through services.write with key redaction (V9).
b3_requirements.fail_if: Any unlisted change outside these bounds, or a new unredacted write.

b3_requirements.pass_if: Optional: also require envelope status 'collected' and records == trace size, and report journal issued_commands. Success is still no claim of cycles or admission effect.

A2 Pins, checked in a NEW capsule: the frozen bytes equal the supplied hashes, and the before-state hash is verified. These must be unchanged: client 933e4161d4eadd7b9730f4d122387aad15932343bcc18de7580e9ea92b86fe95, metrics 49c76b8bcda2560ed9c24770a41c3fa876082cd0e19d171daf025300452a60ec, gateway 0b1a80ade258d8875ba80a072c4f360bfa5d4a7ac312bd222c0571380b341570, adapter nominal_episode.py 935c2679 (full hash from the Mayor), runtime 2d7a01dbd335297439d31ec00d144db4d4a771b190d8b47a03e1ddd3a5f80959 and permit 05b7d0aebcede0851300ee70e9947e50ea6c94e6bd3ed2dc1283e10c5fcf6503. If runtime or permit differ, the prior V3-V5/V9 facts are named UNVERIFIED and not re-audited.
A3 Read only the diff hunks plus the minimum context each requirement needs; do not reopen the client, metrics, adapter or episode audits.

A4 Record each MUST row as PASS, FAIL or UNVERIFIED, with file:line in the new bytes. The critical rows B2-2, B2-4, B3-1, B3-2 and B3-3 also need a sealed control (or the one witness) that fails or is absent on the old bytes and passes on the new bytes.

A5 The four draft negatives must be active tests or sealed controls that PASS on the new bytes, with their FAIL-on-old evidence retained. A dropped or rewritten negative needs a replacement that fails on the old bytes.

A6 At most one bounded mocked CPU witness (<= 60 s, preregistered, failures retained, no GPU/network/HTTP), used only for a critical row that lacks a control. Priority: (1) B3 early exit with an injected primary exception plus a receipt-write failure; (2) B2 telemetry failure plus a non-idle GPU.

decision_rule.PASS_SOURCE: All MUST rows PASS, critical rows are evidenced (A4) and pins are verified: source acceptance is recommended for the GPU stage. The Mayor decides.
decision_rule.CONDITIONAL: All MUST rows PASS by source, but a critical row lacks a control and no witness remains; the gap is listed.
decision_rule.FAIL: Any MUST row fails, or there is a scope violation (B2-7, B3-10). Report the smallest exact fix.
decision_rule.UNVERIFIED: Never counted as PASS. SHOULD rows never block.
decision_rule.partial: A B2-only disposition may be issued while B3 is pending. It never implies caller or native approval.

nonclaims: Plan only: not acceptance, not a review of the live fixes, and no GPU or execution authorization (Mayor only).

A CPU PASS, lifecycle exit 0 or caller success is not Native qualification, controller cycles, admission effect, or any MPC or performance claim (prior L8; admin POST count null and native_qualification false by design).
Native eligibility later needs exact source pins (B1 PRECONDITION: the Mayor prereg records the full sha256 of nominal_episode.py and of the caller immediately before execution) and live authority.
Native14 remains FAIL. No criteria relaxation (O-1..O-9 still apply).
